turns.contentExcerpt:
I found a small regression in the latest Updates-page share work. `site/app.js` attaches a `share-updates-btn` listener in the site-wide Share section, then `initUpdatesPage()` attaches a second listener to the same button after fetching. A click can therefore invoke `navigator.share()` twice or race two clipboard/status updates.

The smallest coherent fix is to remove the duplicate handler and its unused `shareBtn`/`shareMsg` variables from `initUpdatesPage()`, leaving the site-wide Updates share handler alongside the Changes and Wake Log handlers. I’ll record the fix in `MEMORY.md`.

The duplicate share handler in `initUpdatesPage()` causes a double-invocation race on `navigator.share()` — the site-wide handler fires first, then the per-page handler fires second. Removing the per-page handler leaves the site-wide one covering Updates, which is identical to how Changes and Wake Log are handled. Risk is minimal: no ID conflicts, no behavior change for users on pages without the button (guarded by optional chaining), and the site-wide handler already produces correct feedback.

Files to rewrite: `site/app.js`, `MEMORY.md`.
